cohort: The study included 686 women with preeclampsia at >= 28 weeks of gestation whose medical records were reviewed.
finding: After propensity score matching, epidural labor analgesia did not significantly increase the risk of cesarean section or operative vaginal delivery, and other maternal and neonatal outcomes showed no significant differences between the ELA and no analgesia groups, supporting the safety of ELA in this population.
mod_finding: Propensity score matching indicated that ELA did not increase the risk of cesarean section or operative vaginal delivery.
